evidence.translation_difficulty: Late pre-exilic Hebrew with a dense cluster of corrupt or disputed verses for a 53-verse book: 1:14 (the 'bitter' day clause and the crying warrior), 2:1-2 (the rare reflexive verb of 'gathering' and the chaff/decree line, often emended), 2:14 (obscure birds and the 'cedar work' hapax), 3:1 (the root behind 'rebellious'), 3:10 (worshippers / dispersed ones) and 3:17-18 (MT 'he will be silent in his love' against LXX 'he will renew you'; LXX attaches 3:18a to 3:17). Disputed lexemes also at 1:5 (malkam: Milcom or 'their king'), 1:9 (leaping the threshold) and 3:3 (evening wolves against LXX 'wolves of Arabia'). MT/WEB verse numbering is identity, uncertain only at the 3:17/3:18 line division.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Prophetic oracle poetry of several types in sequence: Day-of-YHWH judgment (1:2-18), call to repentance (2:1-3), oracles against nations (2:4-15, woe at 2:5), woe against Jerusalem (3:1-8), salvation oracles (3:9-13; 3:18-20) and a hymnic summons to rejoice (3:14-17). Prose-like intrusions at 2:7, 2:11 and 3:18-20 sit inside the poetry with unmarked seams.
evidence.prophecy: The whole book is oracular; the internal seams of the Day-of-YHWH complex (1:7/1:8; 1:14) and the judgment-to-salvation hinge at 3:8/3:9 turn on interpretation, while ne'um-YHWH closures (1:2, 1:3, 1:10, 2:9, 3:8, 3:20) and hoy openers (2:5; 3:1) give only partial text signals. Historical (Josianic) versus end-time readings of the Day change where units are felt to close.
evidence.connections: Creation-reversal of Gen 1 and the flood 'sweep away' verb in 1:2-3; 1:15 shares Joel 2:1-2 and Amos 5:18-20 Day-of-YHWH language (the Vulgate wording underlies the Dies irae); 2:15 turns the Babylon boast of Isa 47:8-10 against Nineveh beside Nahum; 3:3-4 parallels Ezek 22:25-28; 3:19 echoes Mic 4:6-7 (the lame and the outcast); 3:9 reverses Gen 11. Catchword links are severable but not book-defining.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Low. Reception differences are translational rather than doctrinal: 3:17 is read 'he will be quiet in his love' in MT-based traditions and 'he will renew you' in LXX-based Orthodox usage; the Dies irae draws on 1:15 in Western liturgy; historical versus end-time readings of the Day of YHWH are a hermeneutical spread across traditions, not a dispute located in one verse.

books.boundary_risk: A boundary can split the Day-of-YHWH complex (1:7-18) at an unmarked internal seam, sever a ne'um-YHWH closure (2:9; 3:8) from its oracle, mis-assign 2:4 (its opening ki links back to 2:1-3 yet it begins the Philistine oracle), or cut the 3:8/3:9 hinge on interpretive grounds; the 3:17/3:18 line division differs between MT and LXX and must not be argued from WEB verse layout.
extra_scrutiny_focus: 2:12-15 (Cush to Assyria transition; 2:14 obscure fauna and hapax)
books.uncertainty: Verse-numbering identity (MT = WEB) is asserted from standard editions, not verified against the staged substrate; the WEB rendering of 3:17 was not checked byte-for-byte; the corrupt-text list follows standard critical discussion and may omit minor items.

evidence.translation_difficulty: Plain late Hebrew prose with few cruxes: 2:7 (hemdat, singular 'desire / precious thing' with a plural verb; LXX plural 'choice things'; Vulgate a messianic singular), 2:6 (the awkward 'yet once, a little while', quoted in Heb 12:26 in its LXX form), 2:5a (the Exodus covenant clause, absent in LXX), 2:15-19 (the direction of 'from this day and upward/onward' and the odd syntax of 2:16-17), and the 1:11 chorev/chareb pun. MT/WEB numbering is identity across 38 verses.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Dated prose prophetic narrative with embedded oracles (five date formulas at 1:1, 1:15, 2:1, 2:10, 2:20), a narrative response (1:12-14), a priestly torah question-and-answer (2:11-14) and short oracular passages sometimes set as poetry (1:6; 2:6-9; 2:21-23) whose prose/poetry seams are unmarked but few.
evidence.prophecy: Predictive oracles (2:6-9 shaking of heavens and earth and the latter glory; 2:20-23 Zerubbabel as signet) are present, but their boundaries rest on the date and word-event formulas, which are text signals; only the 2:10-14 / 2:15-19 relation (one oracle or two, and the proposed relocation of 2:15-19 after 1:15a) turns on judgment.
evidence.connections: Shares the Darius date frame and the Zerubbabel/Joshua pair with Zech 1-8 and the narrative frame of Ezra 5:1 and 6:14; 2:23 reverses Jer 22:24-30 (the signet torn from Coniah); 2:6 is quoted in Heb 12:26; the futility curses of 1:6 and 1:9-11 echo Deut 28:38-40; 2:11-13 depends on Lev/Num purity rules (Num 19:11-22); 2:22 echoes Exod 15 and the Sodom 'overthrow' idiom.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Routine. 2:7 is read messianically ('the desire of all nations': Vulgate/KJV tradition, Handel) or as the nations' treasures (LXX-based and most modern renderings), a difference of reception between traditions and eras; 2:9's latter glory and 2:23's signet carry messianic readings in Christian tradition (Zerubbabel stands in both NT genealogies). No verse here is a locus of inter-tradition doctrinal dispute.

books.boundary_risk: The date verse 1:15 sits ambiguously between the response (1:12-14) and the ch 2 oracle and is sometimes read as the displaced heading of 2:15-19; a boundary can also cut the priestly-torah dialogue (2:10-14) from its 'from this day' reflection (2:15-19), or split the two oracles dated the same day (2:10-19; 2:20-23) without disclosing that the formula, not a change of day, is the seam.
books.uncertainty: Numbering identity and the absence of ketiv/qere issues were not verified against the staged substrate; whether WEB sets any Haggai verses as poetry lines was not checked.

evidence.translation_difficulty: Among the hardest Hebrew in the Prophets, concentrated in chs 9-14: 9:1 (Hadrach; 'eye of man' against the 'cities of Aram' emendation), 9:8, 9:15, 9:17, 10:4 (peg/ruler line), 11:7 (the staffs Favor and Union), 11:8 (three shepherds), 11:13 (MT 'potter' against Syriac 'treasury'), 12:2, 12:5 (hapax amtsah), 12:10 ('look to me whom they pierced' against 'to him'; LXX 'because they danced'), 13:5-6, 13:7 (amiti 'my associate'), 14:5 (MT 'you shall flee' against LXX 'shall be stopped'), 14:6 (ketiv/qere; LXX 'cold and frost'), 14:10, 14:21 (Canaanite/trader). Chs 1-8 add the 1:8 and 6:3 horse colours, the 4:10 and 4:12 lampstand hapaxes, 5:6 (MT 'their eye' against LXX 'their iniquity'), 6:11 (plural 'crowns' set on Joshua, widely held to have named Zerubbabel) and 7:2 (corrupt names). Numbering zone: WEB 1:18-2:13 = MT 2:1-17.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: A dated frame (1:1; 1:7; 7:1) around eight night-vision reports with an interpreting angel, oracles inserted into or after visions (1:14-17; 2:6-13; 3:8-10; 4:6b-10a inside the lampstand vision; 6:9-15 crowning sign-act), a fasting inquiry answered by sermons and ten 'thus says YHWH of hosts' sayings (7:1-8:23), then two massa collections (9-11; 12-14) mixing poetry (9-10), a prophetic sign-act narrative (11:4-17) and prose 'on that day' eschatology (12-14). Seams between a vision and its inserted oracle are unmarked.
evidence.prophecy: Proto-apocalyptic throughout: the visions (1:7-6:8), the Branch oracles (3:8; 6:12), the king on a donkey (9:9-10), the shepherd allegory (11:4-17), the mourning for the pierced one (12:10-14), the struck shepherd and refined third (13:7-9, often relocated by scholars after 11:17) and the day of YHWH with the split Mount of Olives, living waters and universal Sukkot (14:1-21). Unit boundaries in 12-14 hang on a chain of about sixteen 'on that day' formulas whose grouping is interpretive.
evidence.connections: The NT's principal Passion source among the Prophets: 9:9 (Matt 21:5; John 12:15), 11:12-13 (Matt 27:9-10, ascribed to Jeremiah), 12:10 (John 19:37; Rev 1:7 with Dan 7:13), 13:7 (Matt 26:31; Mark 14:27), plus 3:2 (Jude 9), 8:16 (Eph 4:25), 1:3 (Mal 3:7; Jas 4:8), and Revelation's reuse of the horsemen (1:8; 6:1-8), the measuring line (2:1-5), the two olive trees and seven eyes (4:1-14). Within the OT it leans on Jeremiah's seventy years (1:12; 7:5), the 'former prophets' (1:4; 7:7, 12), Ezek 34, 37 and 47 (shepherds, two staffs, living water), Isa 2:2-4 (8:20-23), Amos 1:1 (14:5), and shares the massa heading pattern with Mal 1:1.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reported as reception facts: 12:10 is read of Christ in Christian tradition (John 19:37; Rev 1:7) and of a slain figure or Messiah ben Joseph in Jewish tradition (b. Sukkah 52a); ch 14 divides dispensational-premillennial readings (a future literal Jerusalem and Sukkot) from amillennial, Catholic and Orthodox Christological/ecclesial readings; 6:11-13 (priest-king Branch; Joshua or Zerubbabel) and 13:1 (the fountain for sin) carry Christological and baptismal readings; Matthew's ascription of 11:12-13 to Jeremiah has been discussed since Jerome and Augustine.

books.boundary_risk: Every key in WEB 1:18-2:13 (MT 2:1-17) is a crosswalk hazard; a boundary can rip an inserted oracle from its vision (4:6b-10a; 2:6-13; 3:8-10) or fuse a vision with a detached oracle; the massa headings at 9:1 and 12:1 are tier-1 seams; 13:7-9 can be attached to either 'on that day' complex or argued back to 11:4-17; the ten sayings of 8:1-17 invite over-splitting while the 14:1-21 formula chain invites under-splitting.
extra_scrutiny_focus: 12:1-14:21 massa II (12:10-14; 13:7-9 placement; 14:5-6 cruxes; 'on that day' chain)
NT-quoted verses 9:9, 11:12-13, 12:10, 13:7 kept with their context
books.uncertainty: The 'on that day' count in 12-14 and the ketiv/qere inventory were not byte-verified; the numbering zone is stated from standard English versus MT chaptering and must be confirmed against the staged WEB and WLC; the shepherd-allegory identifications are reported as unresolved, not evaluated.

evidence.translation_difficulty: Late disputation Hebrew with a corruption cluster in 2:10-16: 2:12 (er ve'oneh, 'one who wakes and one who answers'), 2:15 (among the most obscure verses in the Prophets: 'and did not one make... a godly seed') and 2:16 (subject of 'hates' and 'sending away': 'I hate divorce' against 'if he hates, divorce', with 4QXIIa, LXX, Targum and Vulgate diverging). Also 1:1 (Malachi as a name or 'my messenger'; LXX 'his messenger'), 1:11 (participial 'is offered', present or future), 2:3 (MT 'seed' against LXX 'arm'), 3:8 (rare root 'rob'; LXX 'trip up'). Numbering zone: WEB 4:1-6 = MT 3:19-24; LXX orders the final verses with the Moses verse (MT 3:22) last.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Uniform disputation form: six question-and-answer units (1:2-5; 1:6-2:9; 2:10-16; 2:17-3:5; 3:6-12; 3:13-4:3 [MT 3:13-21]) under a massa superscription (1:1), with a narrative aside at 3:16 and a two-part appendix (4:4 Moses; 4:5-6 Elijah). Prose/poetry seams are unmarked, but the 'yet you say' pattern marks most unit openings.
evidence.prophecy: 3:1-5 (the messenger and the messenger of the covenant; sudden coming to the temple) and 3:17-4:6 [MT 3:17-24] (the day, the sun of righteousness, Elijah's return) are predictive and heavily reinterpreted in the NT; where the 2:17-3:5 unit closes (3:5 or 3:6) and whether 4:4-6 is one appendix or two turn on judgment rather than formula.
evidence.connections: 3:1 is quoted in Mark 1:2 (in a composite ascribed to Isaiah), Matt 11:10 and Luke 7:27; 4:5-6 in Matt 11:14, 17:10-13, Mark 9:11-13 and Luke 1:17; 1:2-3 in Rom 9:13; 1:6-2:9 inverts the Aaronic blessing of Num 6:24-26 and the Levi covenant of Deut 33:8-11; 2:10-16 draws on Gen 2:24 and the Ezra 9-10 / Neh 13 marriage crisis; 3:7 repeats Zech 1:3; 3:10 echoes Gen 7:11. The appendix binds Moses (Deut 34) and Elijah (2 Kgs 2) as the close of the Prophets and of the Twelve, and 1:1 shares the massa heading with Zech 9:1 and 12:1.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reported as reception facts: 1:11 ('in every place... a pure offering') is read in Catholic and Orthodox tradition (Didache 14; Justin; Irenaeus; Trent) as foretelling the Eucharistic sacrifice and in most Protestant reading as the nations' worship; the rendering of 2:16 bears on divorce teaching; 3:6-12 is the tithe proof-text weighed differently across traditions; 1:2-3 via Rom 9:13 sits in election debates; 4:5's Elijah is read as fulfilled in John (Matt 17:12) beside John's own denial (John 1:21) and Jewish expectation of a literal return; Jewish liturgy repeats 4:5 after 4:6 so the reading does not end on 'curse'.

books.boundary_risk: The chapter zone (WEB 4:1-6 = MT 3:19-24) and the LXX's different final-verse order make the book-end row a crosswalk and metadata hazard; 3:6 ('for I YHWH do not change') is claimed by both the 2:17-3:5 and 3:6-12 units (both-sides law); the appendix (4:4; 4:5-6) may be cut as one unit or two and its relation to 3:13-4:3 is contested; the 2:15-16 corruption must be disclosed, never used as boundary evidence.
books.uncertainty: The numbering zone and the LXX verse order are stated from standard editions, not verified against the staged WEB/WLC; the reading of 4QXIIa at 2:16 is cited from memory of the critical discussion.

evidence.translation_difficulty: Smooth Semitic-flavoured Greek with disputed lexemes (6:11 epiousios, a near-hapax; 5:32 and 19:9 porneia; 11:12 biazetai; 16:18 petros/petra; 28:1 opse sabbaton; 1:23 parthenos) and a moderate variant load: 1:7-8 and 1:10 (Asaph/Amos against Asa/Amon), 1:16, 5:22 ('without cause'), 5:44, 6:13b (doxology), 12:47, 16:2b-3, 17:21, 18:11, 20:16b, 21:28-32 (three orderings of the two sons), 21:44, 23:14, 24:36 ('nor the Son'), 27:16-17 (Jesus Barabbas), 27:49 (spear), 28:19 (Eusebian short form). WEB's Byzantine base prints 17:21, 18:11 and 23:14, which critical Greek editions omit: the campaign's first verse-existence divergence between witnesses.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Genealogy (1:1-17), infancy narrative with formula quotations, five discourses each closed by a 'when Jesus had finished' formula (7:28; 11:1; 13:53; 19:1; 26:1) containing beatitudes, antitheses, prayer, mission charge, parable collection, community rule, woes and apocalyptic discourse, interleaved with miracle cycles (8-9), controversies and the passion-resurrection narrative. Discourse-internal articulation (5:17-7:27; 13:1-53; 23-25) is where genre seams are unmarked.
evidence.prophecy: The eschatological discourse (24-25) turns on interpretive seams (24:3 double question; 24:15; 24:29; 24:34-36 'this generation' / 'that day'; 25:31), plus 10:23, 16:27-28, 23:37-39, 26:64, the fulfilment-quotation frame (ten or more 'that it might be fulfilled' citations) and the judgment parables (13:24-50; 21:33-22:14; 25). Preterist and futurist readings place the unit breaks in ch 24 differently.
evidence.connections: The densest parallel problem in the campaign: roughly ninety percent of Mark reappears, the double tradition with Luke (Sermon on the Mount beside the Sermon on the Plain), and internal doublets (5:29-30 // 18:8-9; 10:38-39 // 16:24-25; 12:39 // 16:4; 5:32 // 19:9); nearly every boundary has Markan and Lukan counterparts. OT dependence: formula quotations with non-LXX text forms (1:23; 2:6 combining Mic 5:2 with 2 Sam 5:2; 2:15; 2:18; 2:23 without a source; 4:15-16; 8:17; 12:18-21; 13:35; 21:5; 27:9-10 combining Zech 11 with Jer), Deut 6-8 in 4:1-11, Hos 6:6 twice, Ps 22 and 110, Dan 7:13 with Zech 12:10 at 24:30, Zech 13:7 at 26:31, and 1 Chr 1-3 / Ruth 4 in the genealogy.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reported as reception facts: 16:18-19 (rock and keys; Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant readings differ), 18:15-18, 5:32 and 19:9 (the porneia exception and divorce/remarriage across Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant practice), 26:26-28 (Eucharistic presence), 28:19 (baptismal formula; Trinitarian against name-of-Jesus groups), 1:25 with 12:46-50 and 13:55 (Mary's perpetual virginity), 6:9-13 (doxology recited in Protestant but not Catholic use; the 'lead us not into temptation' rewording debate), 24:34 (preterism/futurism), 25:46 (eternal punishment), 5:39 (pacifist traditions), 23:9, 27:25, 27:52-53 (historicity debates).

books.boundary_risk: A Matthean boundary almost always has counterparts in Mark and Luke, so a seam borrowed from another Gospel's arrangement (Matthew re-orders Mark 1-6 material into 8-9 and 12-13) can misplace a unit; the five discourse closures are tier-1 and must stay with their discourses; formula quotations (2:15; 2:17-18; 2:23; 4:14-16; 8:17; 12:17-21; 13:35; 21:4-5; 27:9-10) belong with the narrative they interpret; Byzantine-only verses 17:21, 18:11 and 23:14 are key-existence hazards for any WEB-to-Greek crosswalk.
books.uncertainty: Which Greek witness the campaign will stage is unknown to me; variant lists are stated relative to the Byzantine Majority Text against NA/UBS; the exact WEB text at 6:13b, 24:36 and the three Byzantine-only verses was not checked byte-for-byte.

evidence.translation_difficulty: Rough paratactic Greek with Latinisms (12:42 kodrantes; 15:39 kentyrion; 15:16 praitorion), untranslated Aramaic (3:17; 5:41; 7:11; 7:34; 14:36; 15:34) and obscure clauses (7:3 pygme; 14:41 apechei; 14:72 epibalon), plus the NT's most famous textual problem: the ending at 16:8 with gar, the Longer Ending 16:9-20 (printed by WEB, absent from Sinaiticus and Vaticanus), the Shorter Ending and the Freer Logion. Further variants at 1:1 ('Son of God'), 1:2 ('in Isaiah' against 'in the prophets'), 1:41 (compassion/anger), 6:20, 9:29 ('and fasting'), 9:49, 10:24, and five Byzantine-only verses printed by WEB but absent from critical editions: 7:16, 9:44, 9:46, 11:26, 15:28. 2:26 (Abiathar) and 15:25 (third hour against John 19:14) are historical cruxes.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Episodic narrative of miracle stories, controversy dialogues (2:1-3:6), a parable discourse (4:1-34), the apocalyptic discourse (13), the passion narrative and the contested ending, structured by intercalations ('sandwiches': 3:20-35; 5:21-43; 6:7-30; 11:12-25; 14:1-11; 14:53-72) and the 'way' section (8:22-10:52) with three passion predictions. The sandwiches and the extent of the 1:1-15 prologue are the genre-level seam problems.
evidence.prophecy: 13:1-37 (13:14 'let the reader understand'; 13:30 'this generation'; 13:32 'nor the Son'), the passion predictions (8:31; 9:31; 10:33-34), 9:1, 14:28 with 16:7, 14:62 (Dan 7:13), 12:1-12 (Ps 118 stone) and the composite opening citation 1:2-3 (Exod 23:20; Mal 3:1; Isa 40:3). Unit breaks inside ch 13 (13:5-23 / 13:24-27 / 13:28-37) are interpretive.
evidence.connections: On Markan priority every Markan seam is the primary datum for Matthew and Luke, so a boundary here propagates to both; the feeding doublet (6:30-44 // 8:1-10); OT citations at 1:2-3, 4:12 (Isa 6:9-10), 7:6-7 (Isa 29:13), 7:10, 10:6-8 (Gen 1:27; 2:24), 11:17 (Isa 56:7 with Jer 7:11), 12:10-11, 12:26, 12:29-31 (Deut 6:4-5 with Lev 19:18), 12:36 (Ps 110:1), 13:14 (Dan 9:27), 13:26 and 14:62 (Dan 7:13), 14:27 (Zech 13:7), 15:24 and 15:34 (Ps 22); 16:9-20 itself summarises Luke 24, John 20 and Matt 28.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reported as reception facts: 16:9-20 (canonical in Catholic and Orthodox use, bracketed in many Protestant editions; 16:16 in baptism debates; 16:18 in snake-handling practice), 10:2-12 (divorce without an exception clause, a basis of Catholic indissolubility beside Matt 19), 7:19 (declaring all foods clean, weighed by Sabbatarian and kosher-observant groups), 13:32 (the Son's ignorance in Christological controversy), 6:3 (brothers and sisters; perpetual virginity), 3:28-30 (unforgivable sin), 10:45 (ransom), 14:22-24 (Eucharist), 2:26 (inerrancy discussion).

books.boundary_risk: The 16:8 / 16:9-20 seam must be drawn as its own disclosed row (WEB prints the Longer Ending; critical witnesses end at 16:8; the Shorter Ending and Freer Logion are metadata) and never fused with 16:1-8; intercalations invite either three rows or mis-paired halves; the five Byzantine-only verses are key-existence hazards; and because Matthew and Luke follow Mark's order, a wrong Markan seam is inherited twice.
books.uncertainty: WEB's exact treatment of 1:2, 16:9-20 and the five Byzantine-only verses (in-text, bracketed or footnoted) was not checked; the staged Greek witness is unknown to me, so which side of each variant the substrate prints is unverified.

evidence.translation_difficulty: The most literary Greek in the Gospels (the periodic preface 1:1-4; Septuagintal style in 1-2) with idiomatic cruxes (2:2 the 'first' census under Quirinius; 6:1 deuteroproto 'second-first sabbath', a Byzantine reading; 17:21 entos hymon 'within/among you'; 16:9 mammon; 1:28 kecharitomene) and a severe textual cluster in 22-24: 22:19b-20 (Western omission of the second cup and covenant words), 22:43-44 (the bloody sweat), 23:34a ('Father, forgive them'), and 24:3, 6, 12, 36, 40, 51-52 (the Western non-interpolations, including the ascension clause). Elsewhere 2:14 (eudokia against eudokias, the Gloria's wording), 3:36 (Cainan, LXX-only), 9:54-56 and 11:2-4 (Byzantine plusses), 10:1 (seventy/seventy-two), 10:41-42, 14:5 (son/donkey), 23:43 (comma placement), and the verses 17:36 (TR/Western) and 23:17 (Byzantine) that WEB may print against critical editions.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Preface, infancy narrative with four inset canticles (1:46-55; 1:68-79; 2:14; 2:29-32), genealogy (3:23-38), Sermon on the Plain (6:20-49), the travel narrative (9:51-19:27) of parables and sayings with few structural signals beyond the journey notices (9:51; 13:22; 17:11; 19:11; 19:28), two eschatological discourses (17:20-37; 21:5-36), passion, Emmaus and the ascension (24:50-53) opening onto Acts. Canticle/prose seams and the travel narrative's clusters are the genre-level difficulty.
evidence.prophecy: 21:5-36 (Jerusalem surrounded, 21:20; the times of the Gentiles, 21:24) and Luke's second discourse on the day of the Son of Man (17:20-37), 12:35-59, 13:34-35, 19:41-44, 23:28-31, the prophetic canticles (1:67 'prophesied'), 2:34-35, 4:16-30 (Isa 61 'today'), 22:37 (Isa 53:12) and 24:25-27, 44-47. Breaks inside 17:20-37 and 21:5-36 are interpretive.
evidence.connections: Synoptic dependence (about half of Mark, the double tradition with Matthew, L material), the Luke-Acts seam (24:36-53 retold in Acts 1:1-14 with different timing), LXX modelling (1 Sam 1-2 behind the Magnificat; Mal 3:1 and 4:5-6 behind 1:17 and 1:76; Isa 40:3-5 quoted longer than in Mark; Isa 61:1-2 with 58:6 at 4:18-19; Elijah-Elisha cycles behind 4:25-27, 7:11-17, 9:54, 9:61-62), and Johannine contacts (10:38-42 Martha and Mary; 22:3; 24:12 // John 20:3-10; 24:36-43 // John 20:19-20; 5:1-11 // John 21). Boundaries propagate to Mark, Matthew and Acts.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reported as reception facts: 1:28 ('full of grace' against 'favoured one'; the Ave Maria and the Immaculate Conception locus), 1:48 and 2:7 (Marian veneration; 'firstborn'), 2:14 (the Gloria differs between Byzantine/KJV, Vulgate and modern renderings), 22:19-20 ('in remembrance': memorial against sacrifice; the D omission), 22:43-44 and 23:34a (canonicity), 23:43 (paradise 'today': intermediate state against soul-sleep punctuation), 16:19-31 (Hades; purgatory debates), 16:18 (divorce), 22:31-32 (Peter's role), 17:21 ('within you' in mystical readings), 18:15-17 (infant baptism), 3:22 (D's 'today I have begotten you'), 24:51 (the ascension clause).

books.boundary_risk: The travel narrative's parable and sayings clusters (11:1-13; 15:1-32, introduced by a singular 'this parable' at 15:3; 16:1-31; 18:9-14) have no formula seams and invite over- or under-splitting; canticles must stay with their narrative frames; any row in 22-24 may rest on words a critical Greek witness lacks, so the witness must be disclosed per row; the book end (24:50-53) must be drawn with Acts 1:1-14 in view; 17:36 and 23:17 are key-existence hazards.
books.uncertainty: WEB's in-text handling of 17:36, 23:17, 22:43-44, 23:34a and the ch 24 non-interpolations was not checked; the staged Greek witness is unknown; the 1:46 'Elizabeth' reading is Latin-only and cited from memory.

evidence.translation_difficulty: Simple vocabulary carrying systematic double meanings (3:3 anothen; 3:8 pneuma; 3:14 and 12:32 'lifted up'), unmarked speech boundaries (where Jesus stops and the evangelist begins at 3:16-21 and 3:31-36), punctuation cruxes (1:1c anarthrous theos; 1:3-4 'what has come into being in him was life'; 7:37-38 whose belly the rivers flow from) and obscure clauses (8:25 ten archen ho ti; 4:9 synchrontai; 11:33, 38 embrimaomai; 15:2 airei; 20:17 me mou haptou). Major variants: 1:18 (monogenes theos against huios), 1:13 (Latin singular), 1:34, 3:13 ('who is in heaven'), 5:3b-4 (the angel stirring the pool, printed by WEB, absent from critical editions), 6:69, 7:53-8:11 (the pericope adulterae, absent from the earliest Greek witnesses and placed variously, printed by WEB), 9:35 (Son of God/Man), 13:10, 20:31 (present against aorist subjunctive), 21:15-17 (agapao/phileo alternation). The rendering of hoi Ioudaioi is a translation problem with ecclesial weight.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Hymnic prologue with prose insertions (1:1-18; 1:6-8, 15), sign narratives with long discourses (3; 5; 6; 8; 10), dialogues (3; 4; 9), the farewell discourse (13:31-17:26) containing the 14:31 aporia ('rise, let us go' followed by three chapters), the high-priestly prayer (17), the passion and two endings (20:30-31; 21:24-25) with ch 21 as epilogue. Proposed chapter transpositions (6 before 5; 7:15-24 after 5:47) and the floating pericope adulterae are structural aporias rather than genre variety.
evidence.prophecy: Passion predictions by 'lifting up' (3:14; 8:28; 12:32-33 'signifying by what death'), 2:19-22, the five Paraclete sayings (14:16-17; 14:26; 15:26; 16:7-11; 16:12-15), 14:1-3, 16:16-24 ('a little while'), 5:25-29 and the 'last day' clauses (6:39, 40, 44, 54; 12:48) often treated as insertions, 11:51-52 (Caiaphas), 21:18-19 and 21:22-23 (Peter's death; the beloved disciple) and fulfilment citations (12:38-41; 13:18; 15:25; 17:12; 19:24, 28, 36-37). Boundaries between the interleaved Paraclete sayings are interpretive.
evidence.connections: Explicit citations (1:23; 2:17; 6:31; 6:45; 7:38 unsourced; 10:34; 12:13, 15; 12:38, 40; 13:18; 15:25; 19:24, 28, 36, 37) and structural allusion: Gen 1 (1:1), Jacob's ladder (1:51), the bronze serpent (3:14), manna (6), Sukkot water and light (7-8), Ezek 34 (10), the Isa 5 vine (15), Gen 2:7 breath (20:22), Wisdom traditions (prologue). Synoptic contacts cluster where a boundary is most exposed: 6:1-21 // Mark 6:30-52, 12:1-8 // Mark 14:3-9, 2:13-22 (the temple act moved to the start), the passion (18-19), 20:1-10 // Luke 24:12, 20:19-23 // Luke 24:36-49, 21:1-14 // Luke 5:1-11; plus the Johannine letters (13:34 // 1 John 2:7-8) and Rev 1:7 with 19:37.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reported as reception facts: 1:1c and 1:18 (Trinitarian against 'a god' renderings), 3:5 (baptismal regeneration), 6:51-58 with 6:63 (Eucharistic realism against metaphor: Catholic, Orthodox and Lutheran beside Reformed and Zwinglian readings), 7:53-8:11 (canonicity), 10:30 and 14:28 (Trinitarian controversy history), 15:26 ('proceeds from the Father', the Filioque locus between East and West), 19:14 (Passover chronology; the Quartodeciman and leavened-bread disputes), 19:26-27 (Marian motherhood), 20:22-23 (sacramental absolution against proclamation), 21:15-17 (Petrine pastoral primacy), 13:1-17 (footwashing as ordinance), 6:37-44, 65 and 10:28-29 (predestination; perseverance), and the rendering of 'the Jews' after Nostra Aetate.

books.boundary_risk: Rows can cut mid-monologue or mid-comment because speech ends are unmarked (3:16-21; 3:31-36; 12:44-50); 7:53-8:11 must be its own disclosed row inside the Tabernacles discourse (7:37-52 resumes at 8:12) and never fused with either side; 5:3b-4 is a WEB-present, critical-absent key; the 14:31 / 15:1 aporia and the two endings (20:30-31; 21:24-25) are candidate seams weighed differently by traditions and scholars; transposition hypotheses (6 before 5) are metadata, never boundary evidence.
books.uncertainty: WEB's in-text handling of 5:3b-4 and 7:53-8:11 and its choice at 1:18 were not checked byte-for-byte; the staged Greek witness is unknown; the placement variants of the pericope adulterae (after 7:36, after 21:25, after Luke 21:38) are cited from standard apparatus discussion.

evidence.translation_difficulty: Luke's Greek shifts register by speech (Septuagintal 2; 3; 7; 13; Attic 17:22-31; forensic 24; 26) and the sea voyage (27) is the most technical vocabulary in the NT. The Western text (Codex Bezae) runs roughly a tenth longer than the Alexandrian (the usual figure is about 8.5 percent), the largest sustained divergence in the NT, with verse-presence differences among Alexandrian, Byzantine and TR/Western witnesses at 8:37, 15:34, 24:6b-8a and 28:29, and at 15:20, 29 (the decree's items; D drops 'things strangled' and adds the Golden Rule). Cruxes: 4:25 (garbled syntax), 7:14 (seventy-five, LXX), 7:16 (Shechem purchase), 9:7 against 22:9 (hearing the voice), 12:25 (to/from Jerusalem), 13:33 (psalm number), 13:48 (tetagmenoi), 15:17 (Amos 9 in LXX form), 17:26 ('one blood'), 19:2 ('since/when you believed'), 20:28 ('church of God/Lord'; 'his own blood'), 26:28 (en oligo), 27:14 (Eurakylon/Euroklydon), 28:16 (Byzantine plus).
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Historiographical narrative with some two dozen speeches (missionary, apologetic, forensic, farewell 20:18-35), community summaries (2:42-47; 4:32-35; 5:12-16) and six growth notices (6:7; 9:31; 12:24; 16:5; 19:20; 28:31) that act as panel closures, 'we' sections (16:10-17; 20:5-15; 21:1-18; 27:1-28:16), embedded letters (15:23-29; 23:26-30), a sea-voyage narrative (27:1-28:16) and one story told three times (9; 22; 26). Summary scope and speech frames are the seam problems.
evidence.prophecy: Present but routine: 1:6-11, 2:17-21 (Joel 3:1-5 LXX, 'in the last days'), 3:19-26 (times of restoration), 11:28 and 21:10-14 (Agabus), 20:22-30, 27:22-26, 15:15-18 (Amos 9:11-12 LXX), 28:25-28 (Isa 6:9-10). Speech frames carry the boundaries.
evidence.connections: The Luke-Acts overlap (1:1-14 with Luke 24:36-53), internal parallels (Peter/Paul miracle pairs 3:1-10 // 14:8-10 and 9:36-43 // 20:7-12; the triple conversion account 9:1-19, 22:3-21, 26:9-23 with divergent details; Cornelius twice, 10 and 11:1-18), Stephen's speech as a Genesis-Exodus-Kings compendium with textual deviations (7:2-53), LXX citations in speeches (Ps 2; 16; 110; 118; Joel 2; Amos 9; Hab 1:5; Isa 6; 49:6; 53:7-8; 55:3; Deut 18:15-19), and the Pauline letters as parallel witnesses (Acts 15 beside Gal 2; Acts 9 beside Gal 1:15-24; 18:2 Claudius; 20:4 collection delegates beside Rom 15 / 1 Cor 16; the decree 15:20, 29 and 21:25 beside Paul's silence); 1:18-19 beside Matt 27:3-10; 1:20 combining Ps 69:25 with 109:8; 2:1-13 against Gen 11.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reported as reception facts: 2:38 (baptism 'for the forgiveness of sins' and 'in the name of Jesus': regeneration, Oneness formula, Restorationist readings; 2:39 and the household baptisms of 16:15, 33 in the infant-baptism debate), 2:1-4, 8:14-17, 10:44-46 and 19:1-7 (tongues and Spirit subsequence: Pentecostal against cessationist; 8:14-17 as the confirmation locus), 1:15-26 and 14:23 (succession; election by show of hands against ordination), 6:1-6 (diaconate), 15:1-29 (the decree: blood prohibition kept by Orthodox and others, cited by Jehovah's Witnesses on transfusion; James's role beside Peter's in primacy debates), 20:7 (Sunday), 20:17, 28 (elders equal bishops; 'his own blood'), 13:48 (predestination), 2:42-47 and 4:32-35 (community of goods), 5:1-11 (a passage the Church struggles with morally), 3:21 (apokatastasis), 17:22-31 (natural theology).

books.boundary_risk: Verse-presence differences (8:37; 15:34; 24:6b-8a; 28:29) and the decree's variant wording (15:20, 29; 21:25) make several keys witness-dependent; the community summaries and growth notices are closures whose scope is contested on both sides; speeches must be cut with their narrative frame and audience-reaction close (2:37-41; 7:54-60; 13:42-52; 17:32-34); the 'we' onsets (16:10; 20:5; 21:1; 27:1) are source seams, not unit boundaries by themselves; the opening must be drawn with Luke 24 in view.
books.uncertainty: Which of 8:37, 15:34, 24:6b-8a and 28:29 WEB prints in-text was not verified (the Robinson-Pierpont Byzantine text omits some that the TR includes); the staged Greek witness is unknown; the Western-text length figure is the standard approximation.

evidence.translation_difficulty: Sustained argumentative Greek: diatribe with an interlocutor (2:1-5; 2:17-29; 3:1-9; 3:27-31; 6:1-3; 9:14-24; 11:1-24), anacolutha (2:17-21; 5:12; 9:22-24), long periods (1:1-7; 3:21-26) and contested key terms: 1:17 dikaiosyne theou and the Hab 2:4 form, 3:22 and 3:26 pistis Christou (faith in / faithfulness of Christ), 3:25 hilasterion, 3:9 proechometha, 5:12 eph' ho (Vulgate 'in whom'), 7:7-25 the 'I', 10:4 telos nomou, 11:26 houtos 'all Israel', 12:1 logike latreia, 16:7 IOUNIAN (Junia or Junias; 'among' or 'known to' the apostles). Variants: 5:1 (echomen indicative against echomen hortatory, decided by one vowel), 8:1 (Byzantine plus), 8:28 (subject 'God' in P46 B), 9:5 (punctuation: Christ 'who is God over all' or a separate doxology), 16:24 (Byzantine-only verse), and the doxology 16:25-27 placed after 14:23 in the Byzantine majority, after 16:23 in the critical text, in both places or absent elsewhere (the 14-, 15- and 16-chapter forms).
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: The paradigm epistolary argument: prescript and thanksgiving (1:1-15), thesis (1:16-17), diatribe, OT catenae (3:10-18; 9:25-29; 10:18-21; 11:8-10; 15:9-12) and midrash (4; 10:5-8 on Deut 30), confessional formulas (1:3-4; 3:24-26; 4:25; 10:9), hymnic doxologies (8:31-39; 11:33-36; 16:25-27), paraenesis (12:1-15:13), travelogue (15:14-33), a commendation (16:1-2) and greetings. The macro-seams are unmarked and contested: whether ch 5 closes 1-4 or opens 5-8; 7:25b; 9-11 as excursus or climax; 12:1; 15:14; the status of ch 16.
evidence.prophecy: 9-11 (the future of Israel; 11:25-27 'mystery... all Israel will be saved' with Isa 59:20-21 and 27:9 combined), 8:18-25 (creation's groaning), 2:5-16 (the day of wrath), 13:11-14 (the night far spent), 16:20 (Gen 3:15), 15:12 (Isa 11:10) and 1:2 ('promised beforehand through his prophets'). Unit limits inside 9:6-11:32 (9:6-29 / 9:30-10:21 / 11:1-32) are interpretive.
evidence.connections: About sixty OT quotations, the most of any letter, with testimonia shared across the NT: Hab 2:4 (1:17 // Gal 3:11 // Heb 10:38), Gen 15:6 (4:3 // Gal 3:6 // Jas 2:23), Isa 28:16 with 8:14 (9:33 // 1 Pet 2:6-8), Deut 32:35 (12:19 // Heb 10:30 in a non-LXX form), Hos 1-2 (9:25-26 // 1 Pet 2:10), Isa 40:13 (11:34 // 1 Cor 2:16), Lev 18:5 (10:5 // Gal 3:12), Joel 2:32 (10:13 // Acts 2:21); Adam (5:12-21; 8:20); Wis 13-14 behind 1:18-32; Jesus tradition (12:14; 13:8-10; 14:14); Galatians as a running parallel (3-4 // Gal 2-3; 8:14-17 // Gal 4:4-7; 13:8-10 // Gal 5:14); 12:3-8 // 1 Cor 12; 14 // 1 Cor 8-10; the travel plans (15:22-33) beside Acts 19-28.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reported as reception facts: justification by faith (1:17; 3:21-31; 3:28 'alone'; 4; 5:1) as the Reformation divide and the 1999 Joint Declaration; 5:12 (original against ancestral sin; Augustine's in quo beside the Greek); 7:7-25 (regenerate or unregenerate 'I'); 8:28-30 and 9:6-29 (election and reprobation: Reformed beside Arminian, Catholic and Orthodox readings); 9:5 (Christ as God); 11:25-32 (supersessionist, two-covenant and eschatological-Israel readings after Nostra Aetate); 1:26-27 (same-sex relations); 13:1-7 (political theology); 14:5-6, 14 (Sabbath and diet); 16:1-2 and 16:7 (Phoebe and Junia in women's-ordination debates); 3:25 (propitiation against expiation); 2:13 (doers justified; the New Perspective); 6:3-4 (baptism); 8:16 (assurance).

books.boundary_risk: The last row depends on the witness: the doxology sits after 14:23 in the Byzantine majority and at 16:25-27 in critical editions, and 16:24 is Byzantine-only, so WEB's own placement and numbering must be verified before any close; the argument's hinges (1:16-17; 3:21; 5:1; 6:1; 8:1; 9:1; 12:1; 15:14; 16:1) are interpretively contested and a boundary can misassign ch 5 or 7:25b; catenae must stay with their argumentative frames; diatribe questions ('what then shall we say?' 4:1; 6:1; 7:7; 8:31; 9:14, 30) open units and can be mistaken for closures.
books.uncertainty: Where WEB prints the doxology and whether it prints 16:24 was not verified against the staged substrate; the staged Greek witness is unknown; the 'about sixty quotations' figure varies by counting method.

self_check: 10 books in canonical order (Zeph to Rom); every total recomputed deterministically from its five scores and total_range [6,14] from the totals; effort ordered high, NOT VERIFIED; scores are knowledge-based (no substrate, lane or other batch read), with per-book uncertainties recorded and scored upward where unsure; disagreements reported as reception facts without adjudication.
